subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Rollover Crash Engineering
description: A quick win: understand Rollover Crash Engineering.

hook.text: SUVs with high centers of gravity were infamous for flipping during emergency swerves.

buildup.text: A rollover strips away every safety layer—the roof caves in, belts strain, airbags misfire.

discovery.text: Engineers strengthened roof pillars and launched electronic stability control to stop rollovers.

twist.text: ESC was so effective it cut single-vehicle crash deaths by roughly 50 percent in SUVs.

climax.text: Since 2012, every new car sold in the US must include electronic stability control by law.

punchline.text: The best rollover protection stops the roll before it starts.

quiz.question: What technology most effectively prevents SUV rollovers?

details.summary: Rollover crashes are among the deadliest accident types. Engineers counter them with lower centers of gravity, electronic stability control, and reinforced roof structures that resist crushing.
details.whyItMatters: Rollovers account for a disproportionate share of vehicle fatalities. Advances in roof strength standards and ESC technology have significantly reduced rollover deaths over the past two decades.
takeaways: Taller vehicles like SUVs have higher rollover risk
ESC prevents the loss of control that triggers most rollovers
Stronger roofs protect occupants if a rollover does occur

faq.question: Why are SUVs more likely to roll over than sedans?
faq.answer: SUVs have a higher center of gravity relative to their track width, making them more susceptible to tipping during sharp turns or when tires catch a soft shoulder. Modern ESC greatly reduces this risk.

faq.question: How is roof strength tested in modern safety standards?
faq.answer: A metal plate is pressed against the roof at a controlled rate. The roof must withstand a force equal to at least three times the vehicle's weight before crushing more than five inches.
